newsitem.title: USA: Harcourt sees $236 mln Q3 charge in NEC deal.
newsitem.headline: Harcourt sees $236 mln Q3 charge in NEC deal.

text.p: Harcourt General Inc said Friday that it will take two non-recurring charges against its earnings for the third quarter ending July 31, in connection with the acquisition of National Education Corp last month.

The company said it expects to record a non-cash charge of about $190 million, primarily for the value of purchased in-process research and development, as well as a mostly non-cash charge of betwen $75 million and $85 million for the integration of NEC's businesses.
These charges will total about $236 million, or $3.30 per share, after tax.
The company also said the NEC acquisition will create about $700 million in goodwill based on a cash purchase price of $854 million.

Harcourt said the required amortization of this goodwill and other intangible assets acquired is expected to reduce reported earnings by a further $106 million in 1997 and by $71 million in 1998, $46 million in 1999, $26 million in 2000, $26 million in 2001 and $21 million in 2002.

As a result of these charges, Harcourt chief executive Richard Smith said in a statement that, "The resulting non-recurring charges will create a loss in the third quarter, and ongoing goodwill amortization will reduce reported earnings in the future, but have no effect on cash flow.

"As previously indicated, the company expects reported earnings in 1998 will be diluted by approximately 10 percent to 15 percent due to amortization expenses associated with the NEC acquisition. However, we expect the NEC acquisition to be accretive in the following years."
